items.prompt: Which statement about magnets is true?

options.text: Magnets attract some materials, not all metals; poles can attract or repel.

items.explanation: A magnet pulls some materials, like iron, but not all metals or all objects. Its poles can pull together or push apart.

items.prompt: Which object might a magnet pull?
items.explanation: Iron is a material magnets pull strongly. Plastic and rubber are not attracted.

items.prompt: Which statement about magnets is NOT true?
items.explanation: Magnets pull some metals, like iron, but not all metals. Iron objects can be attracted, and like poles repel.
Two north poles push each other away — like poles repel. Not all metals are magnetic, and magnets do not attract every object.
A north pole and a south pole pull together — unlike poles attract. Not all metals are magnetic, and wood is not attracted.
